result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You are invited to book an eye check. It is called diabetic eye screening.
It checks the back of your eyes. It looks for damage caused by diabetes (diabetic retinopathy).
This test does not diagnose other eye problems.
It does not replace your regular eye test at an optician.
At the check, the screening team will put drops in your eyes. The drops will make your vision blurred for 4 to 6 hours.

## What you need to do
1. Book your appointment by 15 January 2027. Call 01632 960 377 to book.
2. Bring your glasses or contact lenses.
3. Bring a list of your medicines.
4. Bring sunglasses if you have them.
5. Do not drive until your vision is back to normal.

## Dates and medicines
- 15 January 2027: the last day to book your screening appointment.
- The letter does not list any medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What does "diabetic retinopathy" mean?
- What will happen at the screening?
- When and how will I get my results?
- How can I get home if I cannot drive after the drops?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
